finding: The supply supervisor does not enforce the F28388D operating range, and its release points overlap the regulator tolerances. +3V3/+3V3A falling threshold is 3.124 V nominal (3.04-3.21 V worst case), below the 3.14 V VDDIO/VDDA minimum even at nominal. +1V2 falling threshold is 1.122-1.175 V: the low end is below VDD min 1.14 V, the high end is above the TPS62130 minimum output, so a low-tolerance part resets in operation. Release thresholds (VITN+VHYS) reach 3.29 V and 1.204 V, above the worst-case regulator outputs, so a worst-case board never leaves reset. The rails ramp slower than the PMM minimum slew (3.3 V/1.65 ms = 2 mV/us < 8 mV/us; 1.2 V/1.65 ms = 0.7 mV/us < 3.5 mV/us), so this supervisor is the only thing that guarantees in-spec release.
evidence: docs/datasheets/controllers/TMS320F28388D.pdf (SPRSP14E) p91 ROC: VDDIO/VDDA 3.14-3.47 V, VDD 1.14-1.26 V; p101 7.10.1.2.4: external supervisor required on VDDIO and VDD; p105 SRVDDIO-UP >= 8 mV/us, SRVDD-UP >= 3.5 mV/us, note 6. power-supply/TPS386000.pdf p7: VITN 396-404 mV, VHYSN 3.5 typ / 10 max mV. power-supply/TPS62130.pdf p5: VFB 785.6-814.4 mV (PWM), 781.6 mV min (PSM), fixed versions same %. power-supply/TPS7A20.pdf p6: +/-1.5 %. Calc, 1 % R: 3V3 ratio 7.675-7.948 -> falling 0.396x7.675 = 3.039 V to 0.404x7.948 = 3.211 V; release max 0.414x7.948 = 3.290 V vs TPS62133 min 3.241 V (PWM) / 3.224 V (PSM), TPS7A2033 min 3.251 V. 1V2 ratio 2.833-2.908 -> falling 1.122-1.175 V, release max 1.204 V; TPS62130 Vout min 0.7856x(1+49.9x0.99/101) = 1.170 V (1.164 V PSM), max 1.229 V.
proposed_fix: Make the window fit: 0.1 % dividers plus a supervisor whose threshold+hysteresis spread is <= +/-0.5 % (e.g. TPS3703/TPS389 class), and give the rails headroom: VDD at ~1.22 V (TPS62130 RFBT 52.3k / RFBB 100k, max 1.25 V < 1.26 V) with the 1V2 trip near 1.155 V; 3.3 V rails at ~3.35 V (adjustable TPS62130 instead of the fixed TPS62133) with the trip near 3.17 V. Acceptance: falling-threshold min >= 3.14 V / 1.14 V and release-threshold max < regulator minimum at every corner.

location: SYS-IO-AUX 02_rails U204 TLV1117-33IDCYR (3V3); 08_chain U802 TPS3850G33 (SENSE = 3V3); net SYS_RST_N = CTRL XRSn
finding: The 3V3 regulator tolerance overlaps the supervisor window. The TLV1117I-33 guarantees only 3.168-3.432 V. The TPS3850G33 asserts RESET below 3.143-3.193 V (release up to ~3.22 V with hysteresis) and above 3.405-3.459 V. A board whose LDO sits at 3.17-3.22 V or 3.41-3.43 V, or drifts there with temperature or load, holds SYS_RST_N low. That trips both safety latches, resets both MCP23S17 and holds the CTRL F28388D in reset through XRSn: the module cannot run.
evidence: docs/datasheets/power-supply/TLV1117.pdf (SLVS561O) p7: TLV1117I-33 VOUT 3.168 / 3.3 / 3.432 V (VIN 4.75-10 V, 0-800 mA, -40..125 C). power-supply/TPS3850.pdf (SBVS301B) p6: VIT-(UV), VIT+(OV) = nominal +/-0.8 %, VHYST 0.2-0.8 %; p37 Table 11-1: G = -4 % / +4 % -> 3.168 V / 3.432 V nominal. LMR36015 5 V rail 4.86-5.17 V keeps the TLV1117 inside the VIN condition of that row.
proposed_fix: Use a +/-1-1.5 % regulator for 3V3, e.g. TPS7A2033 as on CTRL: 3.250-3.350 V leaves >= 31 mV to the UV release point and >= 55 mV to the OV point. Alternatively use the +/-7 % TPS3850H33 after checking the minimum supply of every 3V3 load. Re-run the stack with load steps.

location: CTRL-C2000 07-10 cell sheets: U701/U801/U901/U1001 TPS26600 (RILIM 8.06k R701/R801/R901/R1001, CdVdT 47 nF C704/C804/C904/C1004, MODE open); SYS-IO-AUX 02_rails U202 TPS16630 (+24V_GD, RILIM 3.57k)
finding: Start-up inrush exceeds the cell eFuse circuit-breaker threshold for the capacitance the CELL contract allows. 47 nF on dVdT gives 2.46 V/ms (up to 3.3 V/ms worst case). A power board with 600 uF (interfaces.CELL_24V_MAX_UF) then draws 1.48 A nominal / 2.0 A worst case for the ~9 ms ramp, before any load current. The MODE-open circuit-breaker threshold is I(CB) = 12/8.06k + 0.03 = 1.52 A typ (~1.38-1.66 A) with tCB = 4 ms, so the eFuse turns off mid-ramp and retries every 540 ms: the board never starts. All four ports start together off +24V_GD and demand ~5.9 A, above the SYS +24V_GD eFuse limit of 4.69-5.39 A (U202 goes into current limit / thermal regulation).
evidence: docs/datasheets/power-supply/TPS26600.pdf (SLVSDG2G) p7: I(OL) 1.425-1.575 A at 8 k; p9: tCB(dly) 4 ms, retry 540 ms; p21 eq.1/2: I(dVdT) 4-4.7-5.5 uA, GAIN 23.75-24.6-25.5, tdVdT = 8e3 x 24 x 47n = 9.0 ms; p23 eq.4: I(CB) = 12/RILIM + 0.03 A, current above I(CB) for > tCB trips. Calc: 600 uF x 4.7 uA x 24.6 / 47 nF = 1.48 A; worst 600 uF x 5.5 uA x 25.5 / 42.3 nF = 1.99 A. power-supply/TPS1663.pdf p8: I(OL) = 18/R(kOhm) +/-7 % -> 3.57k = 4.69-5.39 A. gen/interfaces.py: CELL_24V_MAX_UF = 600, CELL_24V_MAX_A = 1.0.
proposed_fix: Raise CdVdT to >= 220 nF on each TPS26600: tdVdT ~ 42 ms, 600 uF -> 0.34 A per port, 1.4 A for four. Check the start-up dissipation (~0.5 x 24 V x 0.34 A for 42 ms) against the TPS26600 start-up thermal guidance. Alternatively use MODE = RTN (current limiting) and stagger the ports, or lower CELL_24V_MAX_UF in the contract to what the eFuse can start.

location: SYS-IO-AUX 02_rails U202 (+24V_GD), 09_do U901 (switch A) and U902 (switch B) TPS16630 pin 13 SHDN; drivers 08_chain U808 (DO_PWR_EN) and U811 (CHB_OK_L) SN74LVC1G08
finding: The chain-controlled eFuses fail ON when the logic supply is absent. The TPS1663 SHDN pin has an internal pull-up (2.48-3.3 V open-circuit, on above <= 2 V). It is driven only by SN74LVC1G08 outputs, which go high-impedance at VCC = 0 (Ioff). With 3V3 lost (TLV1117 or LMR36015 failure, 3V3 short), or during power-up before 3V3 is valid, DO_PWR_EN floats high and switch A turns on. CHB_OK_L is loaded only by 470 R + LED (clamps ~1.6 V, at or above the SHDN on-threshold), so +24V_GD and switch B may also turn on. Channel B bias removal and both 24V_DO switches then fail in the unsafe direction, against D-012. The build's single-fault analysis covers stuck outputs only, not loss of the 3V3 rail, and the readback expander is dead in the same fault.
evidence: docs/datasheets/power-supply/TPS1663.pdf (SLVSET9G) p9: V(SHDN) open-circuit 2.48-3.3 V at 0.1 uA, V(SHUTR) 2 V max, V(SHUTF) 0.8 V min, I(SHDN) -10 uA at 0 V; p10 tSD 1 us. isolation-interface/SN74LVC1G08.pdf p1 + 7.3.2: outputs disabled (neither source nor sink) at VCC = 0, Ioff +/-10 uA. Netlist: CHB_OK_L = U811.4, U812.2, U202.13, U902.13, 470 R to LED only; DO_PWR_EN = U808.4, U901.13 only; SHDN pull-down absent.
proposed_fix: Add a pull-down at each chain-driven SHDN net, e.g. 47 k to GND: 10 uA x 47 k = 0.47 V < 0.8 V, and the LVC output still drives 3.3 V. Then a dead 3V3 or an unpowered driver means OFF. Add 'loss of 3V3' and 'driver unpowered' to the FMEA.

location: SYS-IO-AUX 09_do: U905 ch2 (DO2 K_A_MAIN) and U906 ch2 (DO4 K_B_MAIN) TPS272C45D with clamps D903/D904 and D907/D908 (SMAJ36A + SMAJ12A)
finding: The main-contactor coils (TDK HVC43, 24 V, 96 R) are de-energised into a ~15 V clamp (OUT -> -14.1..-15.7 V). TDK requires coil suppression with a clamping voltage of at least 50 V. The low clamp roughly doubles the coil-current decay time, t = L/R x ln(1 + I.R/Vc): ln(1 + 24/15) = 0.96 vs ln(1 + 24/50) = 0.39. That means slower contact opening and longer DC arcing on the contactor that carries the D-019 fault-breaking duty. The TPS272C45D cannot be given a >= 50 V clamp: its VS - VOUT absolute maximum is 48 V, so with VS up to 26.45 V the clamp is limited to about -21 V.
evidence: docs/datasheets/protection/HVC43.pdf p3: 24 V coil 96 R, 5.8 W, pick-up 18 V, drop-out 2 V; p4 'Coil terminals should be suppressed with a surge protection device. Preferably a varistor with a clamping voltage not smaller than 50 V'. isolation-interface/TPS272C45.pdf (SLVSF24C) p7: VS - VOUT -0.7..48 V for versions A, B, D. protection/SMAJ_Bourns.pdf: SMAJ12A VBR 13.3-14.7 V. Drop-out ratio computed for I = 0.25 A (24 V / 96 R).
proposed_fix: Drive the two HVC43 coils (DO2/DO4) with a stage rated for a >= 50 V suppression, e.g. a 100 V MOSFET switch with a 50-60 V varistor/TVS across the coil as TDK specifies, and keep the TPS272C45 for the relays. Otherwise get TDK's written acceptance of the 15 V clamp with the resulting opening time, and re-check the D-019 breaking coordination with that time.

location: CTRL-C2000 13_eth: U1301 DP83822I pin 18 RESET_N, R1304 4.7k pull-down, GPIO119
finding: RESET_N has an internal pull-up (I, PU, 6.75-11.25 k), so the 4.7 k pull-down only reaches 0.97-1.35 V. That is between VIL (0.8 V) and VIH (1.7 V). The PHY is not reliably held in reset while GPIO119 is high-Z (MCU reset and boot), and can start before the MEMS clock is stable, contrary to the sheet note.
evidence: docs/datasheets/isolation-interface/DP83822I.pdf (SNLS505H) p5 Table 5-1: RESET_N I, PU; p9: VIL 0.8 V max, VIH 1.7 V min (3.3 V VDDIO); p10: integrated pull-up 6.75-9-11.25 k. Calc: 3.3 x 4.7/(4.7+6.75) = 1.35 V; 3.3 x 4.7/(4.7+11.25) = 0.97 V.
proposed_fix: Use a <= 1 k pull-down (3.3 x 1/(1+6.75) = 0.43 V < 0.8 V). Have firmware pulse RESET_N low for >= 10 us after the clock is stable before releasing it.

location: CTRL-C2000 14_debug: J1401 (cTI-20) pins 17, 18, 19 (EMU2, EMU3, EMU4) left unconnected
finding: The F28388D datasheet requires the unused EMU2-EMU4 terminals of the 20-pin header to be grounded. They are drawn as no-connects.
evidence: docs/datasheets/controllers/TMS320F28388D.pdf p126 7.10.7: 'The 20-pin JTAG header terminals EMU2, EMU3, and EMU4 are not used and should be grounded'; p127 Figure 7-17.
proposed_fix: Tie J1401 pins 17, 18 and 19 to GND.

location: CTRL-C2000 11_port: AFE outputs P_VAX (U301 ADCINA0/U1), P_AUX1 (ADCINA1/T1), P_AUX2 (ADCINB1/W2) behind the 47 R series resistors
finding: These three balls are DAC pins with a permanent 50 k pull-down to VSSA. With the 47 R output resistor this is a 0.094 % gain error (~3.9 LSB at 12 bit, temperature dependent) on channels whose gain network is built from 0.1 % parts.
evidence: docs/datasheets/controllers/TMS320F28388D.pdf p18 Table 6-1 ADCINA0/ADCINA1/ADCINB1: '50-kOhm internal pulldown ... which cannot be disabled'; p160 7.11.2.3.8 note. Calc: 47/(47+50k) = 0.094 %.
proposed_fix: Calibrate the gain of these three channels in firmware (record it in the pin plan), or move one of them to the free ball ADCIN15.

location: SYS-IO-AUX 08_chain: U805 pin 6 and U809 pin 3 (SN74LVC1G11 inputs) on SYS_RST_N (= CTRL XRSn, 10 nF C202 + 10k R210 || 100k)
finding: SYS_RST_N rises with a ~90 us RC (9.1 k x 10 nF), about 30 us/V. It goes straight into non-Schmitt LVC1G11 inputs whose maximum input transition rate is 10 ns/V, so the gates can oscillate at every reset release and toggle NO_TRIP_A/B, which drive the D-FF CLR and the GATE_EN/CHB_OK gates. The latches stay cleared, so no trip is defeated, but the safety-chain gates operate outside their recommended conditions.
evidence: docs/datasheets/isolation-interface/SN74LVC1G11.pdf (SCES487I) p5 ROC: dt/dv <= 10 ns/V at VCC 3.3 V. controllers/TMS320F28388D.pdf p106: XRSn pull-up 2.2-10 k plus <= 100 nF. Netlist: XRSn = C202 10 nF, R210 10 k (CTRL), 100 k (SYS), U805.6, U809.3.
proposed_fix: Buffer SYS_RST_N through an SN74LVC1G17 (as already done for TRIP_IN) before U805 and U809.

location: SYS-IO-AUX 08_chain: spare trip loop J801, R808 1k from 3V3 to TRIP_SRC, R809 10k + C804 100 nF on TRIP_IN, U803 SN74LVC1G17, Q802
finding: The loop wetting current is 0.3 mA (3.3 V / 11 k), not the 3 mA stated on the sheet, which is marginal for silver-contact flow switches and thermostats (nuisance trips). The loop is a field-wired 3.3 V logic net with no protection. A wiring fault to the cabinet 24 V puts 24 V on the LVC1G17 input (6.5 V max) and drives ~21 mA through the 1 k (0.44 W in 0603) into the 3V3 LDO. A destroyed LVC1G17 can leave TRIP_OK stuck high, losing the coolant/thermostat trip of channel A.
evidence: Netlist: 3V3 -1k- TRIP_SRC - J801.1 ... J801.2 - TRIP_IN -10k- GND, TRIP_IN -> U803.2. isolation-interface/SN74LVC1G17.pdf abs max VI 6.5 V. Sheet note in gen/sys_io_aux.py sheet_chain: '3 mA wetting from 3V3 via 1k'.
proposed_fix: Wet the loop from the isolated or field side (e.g. an ISO1211 input from 24 V like the other DIs), or at least add series resistance, a clamp and a TVS on J801 with a Schmitt input. Size the wetting current to the contact makers' minimum (typically >= 1-5 mA).

location: SYS-IO-AUX 04_can / 05_rs485: U401/U403/U501/U503 SN6505B + T401/T402/T501/T502 750315371 + PMEG4010CEJ, unregulated ISO_x_5V feeding ISO1042 / ISO1410 VCC2
finding: The unregulated isolated 5 V sits above the transceivers' 5.5 V maximum recommended VCC2 at the light loads these ports run at (5 mA preload + idle transceiver). The SN6505B + 750315371 curve gives 5.47 V at 25 mA with VCC = 5.0 V. The local 5 V can reach 5.17 V, giving ~5.6-5.7 V at <= 25 mA. That is below the 6 V absolute maximum, so this is an out-of-specification condition, not a failure.
evidence: docs/datasheets/power-supply/SN6505B.pdf (SLLSEP9I) p9 Fig 6-11: SN6505B + 750315371, VCC 5 V, 5.47 V at 25 mA, rising toward lower load. ISO1042 (SLLSF09) p5 ROC VCC2 4.5-5.5 V; ISO1410 (SLLSF22I) p6 ROC VCC2 3-5.5 V; both abs max 6 V. power-supply/LMR36015.pdf VFB 0.985-1.015 V -> 5 V rail up to 5.17 V with 1 % RFB. Calc: 5.47 x 5.17/5.0 = 5.66 V.
proposed_fix: Add a low-dropout 5 V regulator per port after the rectifier, with a higher-ratio transformer from SN6505B table 9-3 so the LDO has headroom; or clamp the light-load voltage with a preload sized from Fig 6-11 so the worst case (5 V rail at 5.17 V) stays <= 5.5 V.

location: CTRL-C2000 11_port: F1101 MF-MSMF110/33X on P_24V; supplied from SYS-IO-AUX U201 TPS16630 (+24V eFuse, 1.84-2.12 A)
finding: The PTC cannot isolate a shorted port board or cable. The upstream +24V eFuse limits at 1.84-2.12 A. With the CTRL's own ~0.35 A load, at most ~1.8 A is left for the PTC, below its 2.2 A trip current at 23 C. The +24V eFuse therefore current-limits and thermally cycles first. +24V to the whole control card collapses and the controller brown-out resets repeatedly, losing communication and diagnostics, instead of only the port branch dropping out.
evidence: docs/datasheets/protection/MF-MSMF110-33X.pdf ratings table: MF-MSMF110/33X IHOLD 1.10 A, ITRIP 2.20 A (23 C). power-supply/TPS1663.pdf p8: I(OL) 1.84-2.16 A at 9 k -> 1.82-2.14 A at 9.09 k. CTRL +24V load ~0.35 A (LMR38020 1.2 A x 5 V / 0.9 / 21.6 V).
proposed_fix: Protect P_24V with an eFuse sized well below the SYS +24V limit (e.g. a TPS26600 at ~0.8-1.0 A, as on the cell ports), or a PTC with ITRIP < 1.2 A at the maximum ambient. Confirm that the port board's own maximum current fits.
